summary: Security audit and fixes for input.py

vulnerabilities.description: Hardcoded API key found in source (AKIA style). Hardcoded secrets may be leaked via source control.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove hardcoded key; read from environment variables (os.getenv).

vulnerabilities.description: query_users_by_name concatenates user-supplied input into SQL statement (string formatting), enabling SQL injection.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use parameterized SQL queries and avoid formatting user input directly into SQL. Use DB abstraction where possible.
vulnerabilities.replacement: cur.execute("SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username LIKE ?", (f"%{name}%",))

vulnerabilities.description: Untrusted pickle.loads on request data — leads to remote code execution when users send crafted payloads.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Do not deserialize untrusted pickles. Accept safe formats like JSON and validate inputs.

vulnerabilities.description: os.system executed with user input concatenated — allows arbitrary shell command execution and redirection.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Do not call shell commands with unsanitized user input. Use a strict whitelist or avoid shell execution entirely.
vulnerabilities.replacement: validate and whitelist commands, disallow shell metacharacters; implement behavior in Python instead of os.system

vulnerabilities.description: render_template_string called with user input interpolated directly — cross-site scripting (XSS) risk.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use templating safely routing values through context (Jinja auto-escapes) or explicitly escape user input.

vulnerabilities.description: Plaintext credentials stored in source code (USERS dict) – attacker with repo access gains credentials.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Store salted hashes instead using a secure password hashing function (werkzeug.security or bcrypt); store secrets in a secure store or environment variables.

vulnerabilities.description: app.run(debug=True) enables the interactive debugger and potentially exposes secrets or remote code execution when reachable.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Disable debug mode in production (debug=False or controlled by env var).

actions_taken: Saved original vulnerable file as input_vulnerable.py
Removed pickle.loads and accept validated JSON for /upload_profile
Disabled arbitrary shell exec; implemented whitelisted behavior for /run
Escaped user input in templates and used safe rendering
Replaced plaintext password with hashed password using werkzeug.security
Disabled debug mode when starting the app
Added reproducible tests (pytest) that fail on the original and pass on the patched code
Added run scripts and Dockerfile to reproduce behavior on Windows/Linux/Docker and aggregated logs
test_instructions: Run detect_and_run.py or run run_test.sh (Linux/Mac) or run_test.bat (Windows). Logs are saved at logs/test_run.log
